replacements.instruction: Retitle the paper so Agentic CogWriter leads the title while retaining the Cognitive Process Theory of Writing and AI-agent framing.
replacements.before: \title{Revisiting the Cognitive Process Theory of Writing for AI Agents: Process-Level Control for Long-Form Writing}
replacements.after: \title{Agentic CogWriter: Revisiting the Cognitive Process Theory of Writing for AI Agents}

replacements.instruction: Align the Abstract proposal sentence with the revised title by making the revisiting claim explicitly about process-level control for AI writing agents.
replacements.before: Drawing on cognitive process theory, we propose \condAgenticCogWriter, which maintains a shared draft, goals, and process history while a Monitor agent chooses and delegates planning, drafting, or reviewing.
replacements.after: Revisiting cognitive process theory as a framework for process-level control in AI writing agents, we propose \condAgenticCogWriter, which maintains a shared draft, goals, and process history while a Monitor agent chooses and delegates planning, drafting, or reviewing.

replacements.instruction: Align the Introduction theory bridge with the revised title by stating explicitly what it means to revisit cognitive process theory for AI agents.
replacements.before: The cognitive process theory of writing~\citep{flower1981cognitive,hayes1996new,hayes2012modeling} provides a useful abstraction for process-level control.
replacements.after: We revisit the cognitive process theory of writing~\citep{flower1981cognitive,hayes1996new,hayes2012modeling} as an abstraction for process-level control in AI agents that produce long-form documents.
